meta_title: AI Agent Code Editor for Mac vs Cursor, Windsurf | jplus2
meta_description: What jplus2's new Agent mode shares with Cursor, Windsurf and VS Code, and how Sublime Text and Nextpad++ differ. Checked against their public sites.
h1: jplus2's AI agent compared with Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Sublime Text and Nextpad++
lead: On 16 November 2026 the full version of jplus2 gained an Agent mode and the project tools around it. Here is what was added, and how it compares with each editor on its own, using only what their public sites and documentation say.
card_title: jplus2's AI agent compared, tool by tool
card_text: Agent mode, project instructions, @files and approvals, compared separately with Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Sublime Text and Nextpad++.

sections.html:
• Agent mode. The assistant can list and read files in the folder you opened, propose file changes and propose terminal commands, step by step. You approve every one.
  • Changes as a diff. Each change opens with Apply and Cancel before anything is written.
  • Commands in the Terminal panel. Each command waits for Run or Reject, and its output and exit status go back to the assistant.
  • Project instructions. It reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules from your folder.
  • Memories and @files. One-line memories per project, and files attached by writing @name (up to 8 text files).
  • Your own prompts and reviews. Custom commands from ai-commands.json, and reviews of uncommitted changes or pull requests.
  • Gateways. A company gateway with a renewable key, and an import from Claude Code's settings.json.

Full version only. None of this is in jplus2 Lite, the free download.

Featurejplus2Cursor
Agent that reads files, edits files and runs terminal commandsYesYes (its tools list)
Project instructions in AGENTS.mdYes, plus CLAUDE.md and .cursorrulesYes (AGENTS.md and its own rules files)
@ to bring files into the chatYes, @name or the paperclipYes, files and folders
Terminal output as contextOutput of each approved command goes back to the assistantYes, with @Terminals
EditsEvery change is a diff you apply or cancelIts documentation describes edits applied automatically, with checkpoints to restore

The two overlap on the agent loop. The differences are that jplus2 stops at every edit and command, and that it is a native Mac app where you bring the model.

Featurejplus2Windsurf
Agent that edits code and uses the terminal as a toolYesYes (Cascade, Code mode)
Project instructions in AGENTS.mdYes, plus CLAUDE.md and .cursorrulesYes, and its own rules files
UndoOne undo step per change, and nothing is written until you press ApplyCheckpoints and reverts to earlier steps
Step limitStops by itself after 20 stepsUp to 40 tool calls per prompt by default

Cascade is a similar agent loop. jplus2 asks before each step; check Windsurf's documentation for how it handles approval today.

Featurejplus2VS Code
Agent that finds code, makes changes and runs checksYesYes, in the Chat view and the Agents window
Approval for terminal commands and editsAlways: Run, Reject, Apply, CancelPermissions and approvals decide which actions ask
Project instructionsAGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrulesCustom and project instructions
Your own API keyYes, Claude or any OpenAI-compatible serviceYes (BYOK)
Local modelsYes, for example OllamaYes, supported local models

VS Code's agents are broad and extensible. jplus2 is one native app with the assistant built in, and no extensions to choose.

Featurejplus2 (full)Sublime Text
Built-in AI assistant or agentYesNot listed on its website
Extending the editorNo plugin systemPython API and packages, with an expanded API for tools such as LSP
PlatformsmacOS (Apple silicon and Intel)Windows, Mac and Linux

Sublime's website describes a fast editor, not an AI assistant. Third-party packages may add AI features; we have not evaluated them. See also our Sublime Text comparison.

Featurejplus2 (full)Nextpad++
Built-in AI assistant, agent or terminalYesNot described on its website
LicenseProprietary; Lite is freeFree and open source (GPL v3)
PluginsNonePlugin Admin, with Windows Notepad++ plugins being ported
PlatformsmacOSmacOS and Linux

Nextpad++ is a Mac port of Notepad++, not an AI editor. If you want an open-source, plugin-friendly editor it is a good fit; if you want an agent inside the editor, that is what jplus2's full version adds.

Agent mode is part of the full version of jplus2, which is coming to the Mac App Store. jplus2 Lite, the free download, does not include the assistant or Agent mode. Leave your email below and we will tell you the day it is available.

The facts about other tools come from their public documentation and websites, read on 16 November 2026: Cursor (cursor.com/docs), Windsurf (docs.windsurf.com), VS Code (code.visualstudio.com/docs), Sublime Text (sublimetext.com) and Nextpad++ (nextpad.org). A feature marked as not listed means the site does not describe it, not that it does not exist. These products change often, so check their sites for the current state. All names are trademarks of their owners; jplus2 is not affiliated with them. Windsurf is now called Devin Desktop.

faq.q: Is Agent mode in jplus2 Lite?
faq.a: No. It is part of the full version, which is coming to the Mac App Store.

faq.q: Can the agent change my files without asking?
faq.a: No. Every file change opens as a diff to apply or cancel, and every command waits for you to press Run.

faq.q: Does it work with a project set up for Cursor?
faq.a: It reads .cursorrules and AGENTS.md files, so the instructions already in the project are used.
Only when you use the assistant, and to the model you chose. In agent mode, what it reads and what your commands print is sent so it can continue.
